chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Ali ibn Maymoun al-Sa'ig, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about what is swept from the dirt, which I sell, so what shall I do with it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Give it in charity, for either it is yours or it is for its rightful one.' I said, 'Supposing therein is gold and silver and iron, so for which thing shall I sell it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Sell it with foodstuff.' I said, 'Supposing there are relatives for him who are needy, can I give it to them from it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on money earned from selling dirt swept from one's home?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling on 'earth money' (thaman al-turab), advising that proceeds from selling swept dirt be given in charity as a precautionary measure (ihtiyat) since ownership is uncertain. The Imam further permits exchanging it for foodstuff and distributing it to needy relatives, highlighting the flexibility in handling minor, ambiguous assets within Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the principle of resolving doubt through charitable distribution while maintaining the asset's utility for the family.
